title: marchmont volume discount revision
instruction:
Ibrahim, you’re the sales manager finishing Marchmont Confections Wholesale’s first written volume-discount program for owner approval this month. Hartsmere Associates has put the current draft, figures, legal review and our marked comments into `marchmont_discount_revision_packet.docx`. Turn that into a signed schedule that reps can operate and a short presentation containing the exact retailer-ad wording they may release. Sales has been using “net price” for both invoice net and the after-quarter, freight-adjusted result, so the finished materials cannot leave that term open to both readings. We also promised consistent access to the published program, but a verified street-match can put a small account below a larger account’s regular tier; the documents need to remain workable when that happens. Apply the packet for New Jersey sales as of 15 February 2026, reflect the changed freight facts, and keep Rushmere Council’s non-resale account outside the retailer schedule. Put `volume_discount_rebate_schedule.pdf`, no more than four pages, and `retailer_ad_claims.pptx`, no more than five slides, at the top level of the working directory using exactly those filenames. The schedule must carry your approval signature and date, and both files must agree wherever they repeat a figure.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/marchmont_discount_revision_packet.docx` — Current draft schedule, approved commercial figures, changed freight facts, legal review, substantiation records and explicit review comments for the revision.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `volume_discount_rebate_schedule.pdf` — Approved, signed volume-discount and quarterly-rebate operating schedule for New Jersey retailer accounts. (Maximum four pages; suitable for use by sales representatives and retailer contacts; include approval signature, approval date and a concise record of the revision.)
- `retailer_ad_claims.pptx` — Short presentation containing the exact print wording sales representatives may provide for substantiated retailer advertisements. (Maximum five slides; wording and all repeated figures must agree with the signed schedule and supplied substantiation.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

Marchmont Confections Wholesale
VOLUME-DISCOUNT REVISION PACKET  |  NJ operation  |  prepared 24 February 2026
Working packet for owner sign-off. This packet replaces the February working draft only after the sales manager issues the signed schedule. Legal review: federal and New Jersey snapshot current through 15 February 2026 (Hartsmere Associates).
1. Current draft excerpt — marked for replacement
“Net price” means our price after discounts and freight. Retailers buying 240 cases get 10%; big accounts get 15%. Freight support is $18 per pallet. A 2% quarterly rebate may apply. Sales may match or beat a competitor where needed. Retailers may advertise wholesale savings of up to 25%. Rushmere Council is a retailer example.
Review comments: bare net price has two meanings; replace the $18-per-pallet freight fact; say whether tiers are retroactive; state rebate base and timing; remove Council; bound competitive matching; preserve resale-pricing independence; use exact ad copy only; add signature, retention and escalation.
2. Approved commercial facts
Scope and account facts: Sales are to New Jersey delivery addresses only. A qualifying retailer is an active grocery, specialty-food, pharmacy, or convenience-store account with a current resale certificate, buying covered goods for resale from its own retail location(s). Direct-to-consumer, marketplace, institutional, public-sector, distributor and non-resale accounts do not qualify. Rushmere Council buys for events and does not resell; it is expressly outside this retailer program.

The base wholesale amounts are merchandise list prices per display case, before invoice discount; they exclude freight, tax and non-merchandise charges. MSRP is Marchmont’s bona fide manufacturer-suggested retail comparison reference, not a required, minimum or suggested retail resale term for any retailer.
Quarterly completed eligible volume
Immediate invoice discount
1–239 completed eligible cases
5%
240–599 completed eligible cases
10%
600 or more completed eligible cases
15%
Approved tier method: measurement is each calendar quarter, from 12:00 a.m. on its first day through 11:59 p.m. on its last day, based on completed eligible case purchases. The highest tier reached applies retroactively to all completed eligible case purchases in that same quarter. Original shipments invoice at the tier then established by quarter-to-date completed volume; after quarter close, the difference needed to apply the highest earned tier to earlier eligible purchases is a volume credit. Returns, cancellations and credited units are removed from volume and all related values.
Aggregation: purchases may aggregate only under one Marchmont billing account for locations owned by the same legal retailer and enrolled under that account before the quarter begins. Do not aggregate separately billed accounts, affiliates, franchises, buying groups or different legal entities.
Quarterly rebate: after an account completes at least 480 eligible cases in the quarter, it earns 2.0% of its final invoice-net merchandise purchases for that quarter. The base includes only final invoice-net merchandise for eligible covered cases after the applicable tier credit; it excludes freight allowances, freight charges, taxes, deposits, returns, credits and all non-merchandise amounts. Finance calculates by the 10th business day after quarter end and issues a credit memo by the 15th business day. Later returns, reversals, shortfalls or prior-credit errors are corrected on the next account statement or credit memo.
Changed freight fact (approved 15 February 2026): effective for eligible cases shipped on or after 15 February 2026, Marchmont grants a separate $1.20 freight allowance per eligible shipped display case on qualifying retailer deliveries of 24 or more eligible cases to one New Jersey receiving location. It is a credit/allowance, not a change to merchandise list price, and is not included in the rebate base. The obsolete $18-per-pallet treatment is withdrawn.
3. Evidence, controls and legal-review note
Cost evidence: the 10 February routing study supports only a $0.45-per-case handling differential for a full 60-case pallet delivered to one New Jersey receiving dock. It may be used only for that documented delivery condition, separately identified, through 31 December 2026; it does not justify any regular-tier rate or other differential.
Verified competition record: Cedar Grove Candy Pantry (Marchmont billing account 21877) received a written 3 March offer from Larkspur Sweets for the comparable MC-SCB-12 product at $31.50 per case, for up to 180 cases delivered to Cedar Grove, NJ, valid through 7 March 2026. The account normally falls in the 5% tier. This supports only a good-faith response to that specific offer, not generalized undercutting. Sales Operations and Compliance must approve and retain the written offer, competitor, comparable product, price, affected customer and market facts before use. Any adjustment is limited to MC-SCB-12, Cedar Grove, $31.50 per case, the documented quantity, and the offer’s verified duration; it does not alter a published tier or entitle another retailer to the exception.
Availability and conduct: publish the regular schedule to every qualifying account and apply objective conditions consistently. Document actual commercial distinctions; the availability, cost and competition records are bounded factual support, not assurance that every differential is lawful. Retailers independently set advertised and resale prices. Representatives may not condition a wholesale term on any advertised or resale price, promise a nonstandard term, or publish a changed claim. Escalate disputed calculations, changed competitive facts, suspected misuse, and advertising changes to Sales Operations and Compliance before action. Retain qualification, cost-support, true-up and competitive-offer records for 4 years.
Hartsmere review note: The schedule was reviewed against the federal Robinson-Patman price-discrimination framework, including functional availability and the limited good-faith meeting-competition path, as well as relevant New Jersey advertising restrictions and federal deceptive-pricing principles for MSRP comparisons. This is a review of stated facts as of 15 February 2026, not court, regulator or Rushmere Council approval or endorsement.
4. Advertising substantiation — exact released wording
MSRP files dated 12 February 2026 and participating-retailer confirmations support the following comparisons only. They do not establish a retailer’s former price, prevailing market price, government approval, market value, or a consumer saving derived from wholesale economics. Any change in price, percentage, product, period or material qualification requires fresh substantiation and Sales Operations and Compliance approval.
Scenario
Exact approved print wording
SEA-SALT CARAMEL BITES PRINT
Save 20% off the manufacturer’s suggested retail price of Marchmont Sea-Salt Caramel Bites (12-count): advertised price $4.79; MSRP $5.99. At participating retailers in New Jersey, 15 February–31 March 2026, while supplies last.
HERITAGE TRUFFLE PRINT
Save 15% off the manufacturer’s suggested retail price of Marchmont Heritage Truffle Collection (8-count): advertised price $6.79; MSRP $7.99. At participating retailers in New Jersey, 15 February–31 March 2026, while supplies last.
PARTICIPATING RANGE PRINT
Save up to 25% off the manufacturer’s suggested retail price on participating Marchmont confection items: Sea-Salt Caramel Bites (12-count), advertised at $4.79 (MSRP $5.99); Heritage Truffle Collection (8-count), advertised at $6.79 (MSRP $7.99); and Cocoa Nib Crisp Squares (10-count), advertised at $2.99 (MSRP $3.99). Maximum applies to Cocoa Nib Crisp Squares only. At participating retailers in New Jersey, 15 February–31 March 2026, while supplies last.
The range claim’s 25% maximum is achieved only by Cocoa Nib Crisp Squares: ($3.99 − $2.99) ÷ $3.99 = 25.06%, stated as 25% under ordinary cent rounding. Sea-Salt: ($5.99 − $4.79) ÷ $5.99 = 20.03%, stated as 20%. Heritage: ($7.99 − $6.79) ÷ $7.99 = 15.02%, stated as 15%.
Owner comment: authorize Ibrahim Rasmussen, Sales Manager, to issue and electronically sign the revised schedule in March 2026 after these comments are incorporated.

VOLUME-DISCOUNT & QUARTERLY-REBATE SCHEDULE
 Issue 1.0 • New Jersey retailer accounts • effective 15 February 2026
 Legal-review snapshot: Hartsmere Associates review current through 15 February 2026. This operating schedule is not a legal opinion or a regulator, court or
 Rushmere Council endorsement.


 1 PROGRAM SCOPE & ELIGIBILITY
 Eligible accounts. Active New Jersey grocery, specialty-food, pharmacy or convenience-store accounts with a current resale certificate, buying
 covered goods for resale from their own retail location(s). New Jersey delivery is required. Direct-to-consumer, marketplace, institutional,
 public-sector, distributor and non-resale accounts are excluded. Rushmere Council is a non-resale event purchaser and is outside this
 retailer schedule.
 Coverage. Only the following items participate; the Holiday Gift Assortment is excluded.
  Product ID         Covered product                                              Base wholesale             MSRP

  MC-SCB-12          Sea-Salt Caramel Bites, 12-count display case                $40.00 per case            $5.99 each

  MC-HTC-08          Heritage Truffle Collection, 8-count display case            $54.00 per case            $7.99 each

  MC-CNC-10          Cocoa Nib Crisp Squares, 10-count display case               $25.00 per case            $3.99 each


 MSRP. Manufacturer-suggested retail price is a bona fide comparison reference only. Each retailer independently sets its resale and advertised
 price. Representatives may not condition a wholesale term on any advertised or resale price.

 2 REGULAR VOLUME TIERS
  Completed eligible cases in calendar quarter                                      Immediate invoice discount

  1–239 completed eligible cases                                                    5%

  240–599 completed eligible cases                                                  10%

  600 or more completed eligible cases                                              15%

 Measurement and tier operation. Calendar quarter means 12:00 a.m. on its first day through 11:59 p.m. on its last day. The highest tier
 reached applies retroactively to all completed eligible purchases in that quarter. Shipments invoice at the tier then established by
 completed quarter-to-date volume. Within 10 business days after quarter end, Finance issues a volume credit for any difference needed to apply
 the final highest tier to earlier eligible purchases. Returns, cancellations and credited units are removed from volume and related credits.
 Aggregation. Aggregate only locations owned by the same legal retailer and enrolled before the quarter under one Marchmont billing account.
 Never aggregate separately billed accounts, affiliates, franchises, buying groups or other legal entities.




Marchmont Confections Wholesale • New Jersey retailer schedule • Issue 1.0                                                                               Page 1 of 4
  3 PRICE TERMS, REBATE & FREIGHT
 Defined terms — use exactly. Invoice net price is the merchandise amount actually invoiced after the immediate applicable tier discount,
 before the quarterly rebate and freight allowance. The quarter-end volume credit completes the retroactive tier treatment. Effective net price is
 the after-quarter merchandise result: final invoice net price less the earned quarterly rebate and the applicable separate freight allowance. Do not
 use bare “net price.”
 Price basis. The invoice discount is applied only to the base wholesale merchandise list price shown on page 1; it is not applied to MSRP,
 freight, tax, deposits or other non-merchandise amounts.
 Quarterly rebate. An account completing at least 480 eligible cases earns 2.0% of final invoice-net merchandise purchases for that quarter.
 The rebate base excludes freight allowances and charges, taxes, deposits, returns, credits and every non-merchandise amount. Finance
 calculates by the 10th business day after quarter end and issues a credit memo by the 15th business day. Later returns, reversals, shortfalls
 or prior-credit errors are corrected on the next statement or credit memo.
 Freight allowance — revised. For eligible cases shipped on or after 15 February 2026, Marchmont grants a separate $1.20 per eligible
 shipped display case on retailer deliveries of 24 or more eligible cases to one New Jersey receiving location. It is a freight credit/allowance,
 not a merchandise-list-price reduction, is excluded from the rebate base, and reduces effective net price once.

 4 EFFECTIVE-NET CALCULATION
 Effective net per eligible case = base wholesale price − applicable final tier discount − 2.0% quarterly rebate (if the 480-case trigger is
 met) − $1.20 freight allowance (if shipment conditions are met). Components appear once only. Currency is rounded to the nearest cent at
 the displayed per-case and transaction totals.
 Worked calculation — MC-SCB-12. An account completes 600 eligible Sea-Salt Caramel Bites cases in the quarter and ships the cases to one
 NJ location: base $40.00 × 600 = $24,000.00; 15% final tier discount = $3,600.00; final invoice net = $20,400.00 ($34.00/case). Rebate: 2.0% ×
 $20,400.00 = $408.00 ($0.68/case). Freight allowance: $1.20 × 600 = $720.00. Effective net = $20,400.00 − $408.00 − $720.00 = $19,272.00
 ($32.12/case).
 Reconciliation. Finance applies volume, rebate and freight credits as stated above; no return or credited purchase remains in qualification or
 value. Disputed calculations or changed facts: stop and escalate to Sales Operations and Compliance before any promise.




Marchmont Confections Wholesale • New Jersey retailer schedule • Issue 1.0                                                                  Page 2 of 4
  5 CONSISTENT ACCESS & DOCUMENTED EXCEPTIONS
 Published schedule. Sales Operations will make this schedule available to every qualifying account. Apply its objective tiers consistently to
 similarly situated accounts. Actual documented commercial facts may support a limited distinction; do not use account-by-account discretion as
 a substitute for the published schedule.
 Bounded cost differential. The 10 February routing study supports only a separately identified $0.45 per-case handling differential for a full
 60-case pallet delivered to one New Jersey receiving dock, through 31 December 2026. It does not justify the regular tiers or any
 larger/unrelated differential.
 Street-match / meeting competition. A response may be made only in good faith to meet a specific, verified competing offer, not to
 undercut competitors generally. Before an adjusted price is used, Sales Operations and Compliance must approve and retain contemporaneous
 evidence naming the competitor, comparable product, offered price, affected customer, quantity, delivery/market circumstances and offer
 duration.
 The adjustment is limited to the comparable product, affected customer, supported amount, documented quantity and verified duration. It is not a
 new tier. A documented street-match can put a smaller account below another account’s regular effective tier; that fact alone neither changes
 this published tier schedule nor entitles any account to the exception. For the verified packet case only, any match is limited to Cedar Grove
 Candy Pantry; MC-SCB-12; $31.50 per case; up to 180 cases; and the written offer valid through 7 March 2026.

 6 ADMINISTRATION, RECORDS & COMPLIANCE
 Representatives must escalate before promising or publishing a nonstandard term: disputed calculation, changed competitive fact, suspected
 misuse, or any retailer-specific advertising change. Retain qualification, cost-support, true-up and competitive-offer records for 4 years.
 Availability, cost and competition facts are bounded controls or defenses; they do not guarantee that every differential is lawful.
 This schedule reflects the packet’s federal and New Jersey review as of 15 February 2026. It does not claim approval by a court, regulator or
 Rushmere Council.

 7 REVISION RECORD
 Issue 1.0, 06 March 2026: replaces the superseded $18-per-pallet freight treatment with the $1.20-per-eligible-case allowance effective 15
 February 2026; distinguishes invoice net price from effective net price; confirms retroactive quarterly tiers, rebate base and settlement; removes
 the Rushmere Council non-resale account; adds record retention, escalation and documented street-match controls; and confines advertising to
 exact substantiated wording in the controlled claims guide.


                   APPROVED AND SIGNED ELECTRONICALLY                                  Owner issue authorization
                   Ibrahim Rasmussen                                                   March 2026 issuance authorized in packet
                   Sales Manager, Marchmont Confections Wholesale                      Schedule effective: 15 February 2026
                   Approval date: 06 March 2026




Marchmont Confections Wholesale • New Jersey retailer schedule • Issue 1.0                                                                 Page 3 of 4

spec.professional_context: Marchmont Confections Wholesale is formalizing telephone-based retailer discounts after review by Hartsmere Associates. The sales manager has authority to issue the revised schedule for the New Jersey operation and must provide non-specialist representatives with controlled advertising language.
difficulty_sources: Resolving an ambiguous pricing term used for two economically different amounts
Reconciling equal access to published tiers with a fact-specific meeting-competition exception
Calculating the interaction of invoice discounts, quarterly rebate true-up and a revised freight allowance
Converting substantiation into exact, bounded consumer-facing MSRP claim language
Applying federal and New Jersey doctrinal limitations without overstating legal certainty
Keeping a signed schedule and claims presentation numerically and terminologically consistent

reference_artifact.purpose: Create one coherent workplace revision packet containing the existing draft, explicit review comments, changed commercial facts, approved figures, substantiation records and a dated legal-review note.
reference_artifact.jurisdiction_and_snapshot: State that the program covers sales to New Jersey retailer accounts and that the legal review is current through 15 February 2026. Include a concise, professionally realistic review of the Robinson-Patman Act price-discrimination constraints, good-faith meeting-competition limitation, functional-availability concerns, independent resale-pricing boundary, applicable New Jersey advertising restrictions and the federal deceptive-pricing principles governing MSRP comparisons.
draft_defects: The old draft uses bare “net price” in some places for invoice price after the immediate discount and elsewhere for the economic result after rebate and freight allowance.
The old draft carries a superseded freight treatment that uses a different unit basis from the changed fact approved for the new program.
The old draft does not explain whether tiers operate retroactively or marginally.
The old draft presents the quarterly rebate without identifying whether freight, returns, taxes and non-merchandise charges enter the calculation base.
The old draft contains an informal street-match sentence that could be read as broad discretion to beat any competitor.
The old draft loosely links wholesale discount percentages to consumer-facing percentage-off claims.
The old draft includes a non-resale public account among retailer examples even though that account does not resell goods.
The old draft lacks a signed approval, revision record, retention control and clear escalation route.
commercial_relationships: Provide a base wholesale price, bona fide manufacturer-suggested retail price and product identifier for each covered product.

Provide objective regular volume thresholds and corresponding immediate invoice-discount rates. Choose figures that create meaningful but readily calculable differences and make all thresholds available to similarly situated qualifying retailers.
Specify in the approved comments whether the reached regular tier applies to all qualifying purchases in the quarter or only to units above a threshold; the gold must follow that choice.
Define qualifying volume using completed eligible merchandise purchases, with returns, cancellations and credited units removed.

Provide a quarterly rebate with an objective trigger and rate distinct from the immediate invoice discount. Define its merchandise base and explicitly exclude or include freight, tax and other amounts so only one defensible computation is possible.
Provide true-up, credit-memo or account-adjustment timing and a correction rule for prior credits or shortfalls.

Change the freight allowance from the obsolete draft basis to an approved per-unit basis with eligibility conditions and an effective date. The allowance must be economically separate from merchandise list price.

Define invoice net as the base wholesale merchandise price less the immediate invoice discount, before quarterly rebate and freight allowance. Define effective net as invoice net less the earned rebate and applicable freight allowance, with each component counted once.
Include source inputs that permit a worked example to be recalculated exactly under ordinary currency rounding.
Include cost support for one bounded differential. Its value and scope must not justify any larger or unrelated discount.

Include a verified competing offer creating the intended edge case: a qualifying smaller retailer can receive a temporary matched price below the regular effective price of a larger-volume retailer. The evidence must support a good-faith match, not general undercutting.

Limit that competitive response to the comparable product, affected customer, supported amount and verified duration. Require approval and contemporaneous retention of the competitor, product, price and market evidence.
Set a realistic record-retention period for qualification records, cost support, true-up calculations and competitive-offer evidence.
Specify an internal role for pre-use approval of competitive exceptions and advertising changes, without requiring the solver to invent a person.
advertising_substantiation: For selected covered products, provide approved advertised retail prices and evidence supporting comparison to a bona fide MSRP.
Ensure fixed percentage-off claims can be computed from advertised price and MSRP to within ordinary rounding.
Include at least one supported range in which only identified products achieve the maximum, making an accurately qualified “up to” claim appropriate but preventing it from being portrayed as typical.

Supply exact approved claim sentences, including the comparison basis and all material product, participation, timing, quantity or availability qualifications. These sentences are local conventions the solver must reproduce rather than invent.

State that the evidence supports an MSRP comparison only; it does not establish a retailer’s former price, a prevailing market price, government approval or a guaranteed consumer saving derived from wholesale economics.
Require fresh review if a representative changes a price, percentage, product, period or material qualification.
review_comments: Require a clear distinction between invoice net and effective net throughout.
Require removal of the non-resale account from retailer eligibility.
Require replacement of legacy freight facts wherever they appear.
Require the regular program and competitive exception to coexist without turning the exception into a new tier or automatic entitlement.
Require preservation of retailer resale-pricing independence.
Require exact, substantiated print wording rather than a menu of creative alternatives.
Require both deliverables to share identical product figures, dates and terminology.
Authorize the sales manager to issue and sign the revised schedule during March 2026.

schedule: Use every approved regular tier and product fact from the packet without expanding scope.
Apply the packet’s chosen tier method and qualification period.
Calculate invoice net from the approved wholesale base and immediate tier discount.
Calculate the rebate only on the packet-defined eligible base.
Apply the revised freight allowance separately and exactly once.
Calculate effective net by subtracting the earned rebate and eligible freight allowance from invoice net.
Treat the verified competitive response as a bounded, approved exception supported by contemporaneous evidence, not as a replacement tier.
State the legal limitations without promising blanket legality, regulator endorsement or mandatory resale pricing.
claims_presentation: Reproduce each approved claim sentence exactly, with qualifications kept perceptibly connected to the claim.
Use only product, MSRP, advertised-price, percentage and date facts supported in the packet.
Distinguish fixed claims from the qualified maximum claim.
Explain that wholesale discount and effective net figures do not themselves establish consumer savings.
Provide a clear do-not-alter and reapproval control without adding promotional variants.
cross_file_checks: Match every repeated MSRP, advertised price, percentage, product scope and date.
Use the same definitions for invoice net, effective net, rebate and freight allowance.
Ensure the presentation never broadens the signed schedule or implies that the schedule controls retailer resale price.
